sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The Relationships column and the ⏱ millisecond Length feature gave up on the first try whenever MusicBrainz answered anything other than "503 Service Unavailable". Both already knew to keep asking through a 503 burst, but a "502 Bad Gateway" or "504 Gateway Timeout" — which MusicBrainz's front-end returns for a minute or two whenever a new version is rolled out — and a "429 Too Many Requests" from the rate limiter each ended the request immediately and were reported as a settled failure. All three are now retried exactly like a 503: up to three attempts with a growing pause. A deploy that used to leave a page full of ⚠ cells, or a yellow ⏱ button, now mostly passes unnoticed.

An answer that is genuinely final is still taken at face value. A 400 or a 404 is not retried, because asking again would only produce the same answer, and spending three attempts on every one of them would make a bad page slower for no benefit.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: When MusicBrainz says how long to wait before asking again (a "Retry-After" header), that wait is now honoured rather than ignored. It acts as a floor: the pause is never shorter than the normal one, so a server asking for half a second still gets the polite one-request-per-second spacing MusicBrainz asks of every client, and it is capped at 30 seconds so a maintenance window saying "come back in an hour" cannot park a request for an hour. This is the first time the script has read a response header at all.
